title: The Prophetic Interpretation
english: David remembered; on the day of his trouble he sought God. Also Zephaniah cries out: 'Seek the Lord, all you humble of the earth' (Zephaniah 2:3); for having been found, He lifts up the humble, raises them from the earth, delivers them from corruption, and shows Himself higher than the lofty.

The prophet Hosea also spoke of finding; 'In the day of their trouble, they will say, Let us go and return to the Lord our God, for He has struck and healed us; He will strike and wound us; He will heal us after two days, and on the third day we will rise up before Him, and we will seek to know the Lord; as a ready dawn we have found Him, and He will come to us like the early and the late rains to the land' (Hosea 6:1-3). The prophet calls the Jew to judgment; bring the ignorant to trial. Read the prophet and consider the book. Let his own words be brought against him; for they are written by him, even if they are being practiced by me. Therefore, I will interpret the prophetic sayings. Explain how, how, and when this came to pass; for you have been struck, and you acknowledge it, and we also perceive it; but I do not see your healing, nor do I see your cure. On the contrary, the wound is inflamed, the disease has become more severe, and the illness has run desperate toward death.

Since you do not have the prophetic proof to provide the demonstration, I will interpret the prophetic word; I will show the time and the place, and call all creation to witness with divine, masterful wonders.

God has therefore disciplined us, just as He condemned Adam to death when He judged us to eat bread in the sweat of our face, and when He commanded the earth to produce thorns and thistles for us, when, through the first-created, He expelled the whole race from the paradise of luxury. But having disciplined, He healed and having struck, He made us whole. How and in what way? Listen to Isaiah saying: 'Our peace is a discipline upon him; we were all healed by his bruise' (Isaiah 53:5); so that none of the things spoken by the prophet were false. For the following things will show: 'He will discipline us and heal us after two days, and on the third day we will rise again.'

Do you remember the time when you crucified Christ, when you saw his life hanging on the cross and did not believe? You recognize the drama that was done by you and the wonders of the drama, when Christ, naked on the cross, was led as to a wedding. For he had no sin, he did not need a cloak; he was blameless and did not owe anything to be hidden; there was nothing unseemly in him; for he himself shows what is seemly. However, creation could not bear the flashes of the master's beauty, but light overcame light, the sun gave way to the sun, the sensible to the intelligible, the moving to the omnipresent, the one in a place to the one beyond place, the powerful to the powerless, the one moving the night to the one who established the boundaries of night and day.

It was night then; for darkness covered the whole earth, but day ran again from the ninth hour until evening, and again night followed day according to its law, and again day succeeds night. The two-day journey has been completed in order, and the boundary of the prophecy has been reached: 'He will heal us after two days.'

The end then and the next was taken up: 'On the third day,' he says, 'we will rise again.' For Christ has risen, and we have risen with Him. The Savior has come out of the dead, and our race has come to life, just as the divine Paul says: 'Just as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive' (1 Corinthians 15:22). This tomb is a witness, the joy of the living, the calling of the dead. This stone is a witness, which was rolled away and, rolling, cast down all the idols of the demons; not only rolling, but also crushing and thinning, and licking the dust of the cross and from the earth, 'effusing it like steam from a furnace and like steam from a censer' and by the gust and the roar of the spirit.

The women themselves are witnesses, bringing tangible and intelligible myrrh to the Bridegroom, each on the day and night. The white-robed priest, the angel of the church, is a witness, crying out to them: 'Do not be afraid; for I know that you are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified.' But are you looking for the hour? For it is said: 'We will find Him as a ready dawn.' Luke will be able to tell you this also: 'On the first day of the week, at early dawn, they came to the tomb, bringing...'

title: Andreas and the Kingdom Proclamation
english: As the women stood perplexed about the empty tomb, two men suddenly caused them to stand beside them in shining garments, and the women were frightened and bowed their faces to the ground.
The men asked the women, 'Why do you seek the living among the dead?' (Luke 24:5), and 'Why do you reason about life in a way that is foreign to it?'

The one being sought from you is now sitting in heaven, and the one who was touched is resting in the bosom of the Father, for he gives life to all as a loan, and from him, all nature breathes, and in him, moving things move, and constituent things are constituted, and he energizes active things.

The women then went out and met Jesus, and they saw him as the dawn, and they said to him what David had sung in the prophecies: 'For with you is the fountain of life, in your light we shall see light' (Psalm 36:9).

If you say, 'The women found him, but the apostles did not,' and 'How can this be a common gain, and how can what was found be salvation for all nature?', you are seeking pointlessly and accusing vainly, for the women found what they had lost through Eve earlier, and the one who provided the loss also found the gain.

As the prophecy says, 'As the dawn, we shall find him, and he will come to us as the early and late rain upon the earth' (Joel 2:23), which has been fulfilled clearly, word for word, and no interpretation is needed.

He appears as the early rain to the women and as the late rain to the apostles, for he said to the women, 'Rejoice,' and later in Zion, he said to the disciples, 'Peace,' to dissolve their sorrow and the enmity the dragon had planted.

After this, he said to them, 'Peace be with you, for the conflict is with the devil, and the hostility toward him remains; it is necessary that his horn be shattered, that his poison be poured out, that his sting be trampled underfoot, and now I will forge weapons with which war shall be waged against him.'
Thus it was not in vain that Andreas announced to Peter, 'We have found the Messiah, the one called Christ,' because also God had spoken these things through the prophecy of Isaiah (Isaiah 55:6).

Andreas dared to ask Christ, 'I know you have no house on earth, you do not build in corruption, and you do not pitch your tent in brick; where do you dwell?' so that he might become the gatekeeper of the courtyard of the Lord's house, quoting Psalm 84:10, 'I have chosen rather to be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than to dwell with you in tents of sinners,' and he asked again, 'Where do you dwell?' If I learn, I will not depart from the door.
But this now is the church's table set from the gospels, and I, as a servant, have only placed the dishes; therefore, if it seems good to you, I will change to another table.

Andreas' calling crowns him, showing to the soldier the election, and the value of the vineyard worker is demonstrated by the hiring, as presented by Matthew, when Jesus began to proclaim and say, 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near' (Matthew 4:17).

From then on, after he had sanctified the Jordan, planted the gift of baptism, broken the heads of the dragons in the waters, and brought down the gift of the Spirit from heaven, he opened the way of life and lifted up the gate of salvation, and the debtor who wipes away all charges came, and the generous king took up residence.

The judge of the prison is present, freeing the guilty, loosening bonds, and wiping away all charges, veiling his eyes so he may not see injustice, and weighing down his ears so he may not hear the judgment of blood, saying, 'Repent, wash your deeds with the word, cleanse your mouth with your tongue, purify your life with prayer, and bring forward a sacrifice that rules over many,' for the kingdom of heaven has come near (Matthew 4:17).

The one who repents is freed not only from terrible things but also receives the inheritance of good things and is not only free from evil but becomes a farmer of righteousness, and the powerful force themselves, the weak…

title: Repentance and Following Christ
english: We are encouraged to repent, for it is not of the one willing or running, but of the merciful God.
Repentance is a powerful force that can overcome even the darkest of evils, and no evil can conquer it, no poison can extinguish the power of this honey.

The devil may try to wrestle with us, to resist and fight us, but he dare not challenge repentance alone, for in repentance, we find the power to throw off the devil's grasp and escape the tyrant's hand, so we must not trust in ourselves, but in God who straightens the race.

Jesus, walking by the Sea of Galilee, saw two brothers, Simon and Andrew, and called them to follow him, seeing not only their physical bodies, but also their souls, their nature, and their character.

Before Peter had even begun his ministry, he received the reward, before working the vineyard, he received the denarius, before kindling the altar, he received the sacrifice, before preaching, he was crowned, and before evangelizing, the prize of theology was given to him.

The Lord saw two brothers, but now he takes also a second, wanting to proclaim Andrew, the benefactor of Peter, who fulfilled the command which Solomon previously wrote in Proverbs, that brothers should be useful in times of necessity.
Andrew did not neglect Peter when the call was urgent, for he had heard him say, 'We have found the Messiah, the one called Christ'.
Marvel at Christ's ambition, that he chose the poor, uneducated, illiterate, and fishermen to be his disciples, for wisdom does not need co-counselors, but servants.
The Lord gathers his followers from wherever he wants, and he marks them as his own, whether they are prostitutes, tax collectors, or fishermen.
Wherever he throws the seed, the earth bears fruit, and wherever he plants the vine, it immediately grows, and wherever he throws the net, it is found full of fish.
The proclamation of the gospel does not require wise men, for those who wish to partake of true wisdom must become foolish.
Marvel at Christ's wisdom and bless the selection of the apostles.
Consider what they exchanged for what, and it becomes clear from the words spoken to them, when Christ said, 'Come after me, and I will make you fishers of men'.
They had to forget all ancient things and deny their fleshly parents in order to receive the true Father.
The whole world is small to those who follow Christ, being judged by its creator.
When Christ says, 'Come after me', he is leading them to life and to light, to precede the patriarchs and receive the inheritance before the prophets.
Although they may be last, they will become first and superior to those who were hired first.
By following Christ, they will have a life without labor, being rich without money, healers of the world without medicine, and stronger than enemies without weapons.
For Christ is the light of the world, the way, the truth, and the life, and he leads them to the Father, giving them the power to tread on snakes and lions and dragons.
Immediately, they left their nets and followed him.

As Christ said, 'I am the light of the world' (John 8:12), 'I am the way, the truth, and the life' (John 14:6), and 'You shall tread upon the lion and the adder, the young lion and the dragon shall you trample under feet' (Psalm 91:13).
